nodes.summary: For an element $x$ of a group $G$ write $C_G(x)$ for its centralizer. There exist a finite group $G$, an element $a \ne 1$ of $G$ with $|C_G(x)| \le |C_G(a)|$ for every $x \ne 1$ in $G$, and a nilpotent subgroup $H$ of $G$ normalized by $C_G(a)$ (that is, $C_G(a)$ is contained in the normalizer of $H$) such that $H$ is not contained in $C_G(a)$.
nodes.title: Centralizers of maximal order need not contain normalized nilpotent subgroups

nodes.summary: For an element $x$ of a group $G$ write $C_G(x)$ for its centralizer. This is the statement that for every finite group $G$ and every element $a \ne 1$ of $G$ with $|C_G(x)| \le |C_G(a)|$ for every $x \ne 1$ in $G$, every nilpotent subgroup $H$ of $G$ normalized by $C_G(a)$ (that is, $C_G(a)$ is contained in the normalizer of $H$) is contained in $C_G(a)$.
nodes.title: Mukhamet'yanov–Fomin problem on centralizers of maximal order
